gaps.term: nondegenerate subspace and orthogonal complement in F
gaps.quote: A label $U$ is a nondegenerate subspace of $\mathcal F$.
gaps.note: The page never says what nondegenerate means for a subspace, nor that F carries the tensor-product bilinear form, nor what U^perp means (it is orthogonal complement under that form, not the dot product). The projection P_U along U^perp and the dimensions D-1 of U^perp exist only because the lines are nondegenerate (self-pairing 2^3, nonzero), which the page does not state.

gaps.quote: Along a side wire, a label containing $t_T$ may grow to $t_S^\perp$, since $t_T\perp t_S$, adding $h-2$ dimensions.
gaps.note: Labels are subspaces of F=(Q^h)^{tensor 3}, but t_S^perp lies in Q^h and t_T is not a label of F; the paper (lines 945-955, 1048-1055) applies this only to the P tensor factor (P x <t_X> inside P x t_Y^perp), with other factors suppressed. The page gives no assignment of labels to the gates, so the reader cannot see how this relates to the labels U_iota.
